milestones.title: M3 — Evidence and project infrastructure
milestones.description: Establish traceable governance, reproducible correctness/artifact delivery, qualify a real GPU runner and collect matched hardware baselines plus fresh workload profiles. Configuration alone does not satisfy hardware evidence gates.

milestones.title: M4 — Rust ownership and compatibility contract
milestones.description: Select a measured end-to-end CPU pipeline and define authoritative state, command/batch boundaries, read barriers, renderer consumption and API tiers before implementation. Decide from data whether to proceed.

milestones.title: M5 — Integrated persistent CPU pipeline
milestones.description: Implement an optimized JS reference and equivalent persistent Rust pipeline, connected to the retained WebGL renderer, without duplicate JS work or unnecessary intermediate materialization.

milestones.title: M6 — Product performance and release decision
milestones.description: Evaluate the first integrated pipeline's full-path performance, regressions and compatibility across hardware/browser environments. Publish a bounded verdict before broader scene-engine expansion; this is not full-engine completion or automatic npm publication.

milestones.title: M7 — Complete scene evaluation core
milestones.description: Conditional on M6 evidence: extend persistent ownership through visibility, LOD, camera/pass-specific render lists and upload preparation. Preserve shadows, transparency, callbacks and renderer semantics; consume prepared outputs without JS recomputation.

milestones.title: M8 — Backend scope and sustainable release decision
milestones.description: After scene evaluation, profile residual JS resource/shader/backend costs and compare retained-adapter versus existing Rust renderer reuse. Expand only where evidence and compatibility justify it; decide supported release scope and maintenance strategy.

tasks.title: Establish ownership-driven roadmap, Hyper-Waterfall governance and benchmark delivery
criteria: See issue #2

tasks.title: Qualify a real GPU runner for browser benchmarks
criteria: Select a self-hosted GPU machine or separately authorized hosted T4 runner and record cost/ownership.
Record GPU model, driver, CPU, OS, browser, display/headless mode and actual unmasked WebGL renderer.
Reject software, unavailable and unknown renderers; prove the normal workflow uses hardware.
Record whether frame intervals describe a physical display or headless scheduling; do not present T4 as a consumer GPU.
tasks.verification: Successful hardware preflight and browser render smoke, recorded runner manifest; negative SwiftShader rejection test.
tasks.excluded: Paid runner provisioning without explicit authorization; FPS product claims from smoke.

tasks.title: Collect repeated A/A and A/B/C/D hardware baselines
criteria: Predeclare workloads, fixed simulation sequence, viewport/DPR, warmup, sample count, repeat count and noise acceptance rule.
Run A/A calibration separately and balanced A/B/C/D sequences on the same runner.
Preserve all frame samples, CPU p50/p95/p99, intervals, actual duration and environment/artifact hashes.
Separate profiling/GPU queries/startup from primary timing and preserve regressions.
tasks.verification: Complete manifests with matched render work, real Wasm counters, per-run analysis and repeated-session stability.
tasks.excluded: Interpreting historical SwiftShader numbers as hardware results.

tasks.title: Profile representative workloads and rank complete CPU pipeline candidates
criteria: Pin public example sources/assets and distinguish originals from scaled or animated variants.
Profile object transforms, animation/property binding, bone palettes, visibility, sorting and upload preparation where applicable.
Compare many-animated-object/character workloads with original, small/static and GPU-oriented controls.
Estimate useful CPU fraction, expected input/output volume, synchronous read frequency and maximum attainable whole-frame improvement.
tasks.verification: Fresh profiles, attribution method and cost table; select a candidate only after recording rejected alternatives.
tasks.excluded: Preselecting animation or another port solely because it sounds Rust-friendly.

tasks.title: Bound the transform bridge overhead with matched JavaScript controls
criteria: Test reusable traversal storage and semantically safe elimination of overwritten-matrix scans.
Apply identical algorithm/layout improvements to the JS control.
Retain direct mutation, manual matrices, hierarchy changes, force and synchronous read tests.
Timebox by a predefined experiment scope and record a stop decision if full-frame benefit is absent; this is a control, not the long-term architecture.
tasks.verification: Upstream differential/browser checks and repeated full-path comparison including synchronization/materialization.
tasks.excluded: Unbounded micro-optimization or kernel-only success claims.

tasks.title: Specify the measured Rust-owned pipeline and batch cost budget
criteria: Use the reconciled initial conversation in docs/INITIAL_DISCUSSION.md; distinguish user requirements, hypotheses and measured facts.
Choose one complete pipeline from fresh costs, with a finite state owner and minimal boundary crossings.
Define command inputs, stable IDs, intermediate state, output buffers, synchronization points and renderer integration.
Predeclare compatibility tier, useful speedup/noise threshold, regression budgets and stop/pivot criteria before porting.
tasks.verification: Reviewed ADR with cost model, alternatives and explicit go/no-go gate.
tasks.excluded: A fixed commitment to a complete renderer rewrite or one-to-one source translation.

tasks.title: Define compatibility tiers, mutation authority and synchronous read barriers
criteria: Separate import-compatible facade from explicit opt-in ownership API; never silently freeze direct JS writes.
Specify property/matrix identity, direct writes, reparent/attach/remove, updateMatrixWorld/updateWorldMatrix, force and callbacks.
Specify animation events, skeleton reads, object destruction, memory growth, addon core identity, Wasm initialization and TypeScript resolution.
Publish supported/fallback/unsupported behavior and acceptance tests before implementing the new boundary.
tasks.verification: Contract examples and executable test plan against pinned Three.js semantics.

tasks.title: Build the optimized JavaScript reference for the selected pipeline
criteria: Implement the selected state layout, batch API and algorithms in JS with the same inputs/outputs planned for Rust.
Connect it to the same renderer and application workload.
Preserve output/callback correctness and instrument boundary volumes.
Compare it with original Three.js so data-structure gains are not attributed to language.
tasks.verification: Differential/browser correctness plus complete-path baseline and source hashes.

tasks.title: Implement persistent Rust ownership for the selected complete CPU pipeline
criteria: Keep authoritative intermediate scene/animation data in Rust across frames.
Execute the chosen stages in a batch without JS math callbacks or repeated intermediate JS materialization.
Implement the approved command/read/lifetime contract and numerical precision.
Provide counters proving Rust execution and tests proving replaced JS work is skipped.
tasks.verification: Native Rust tests, randomized upstream/reference differential tests, allocation/memory-growth/lifetime checks.
tasks.excluded: A Rust wrapper that calls the original JS calculation.

tasks.title: Connect pipeline outputs to real rendering and validate ownership boundaries
criteria: Prefer the retained WebGL renderer/materials/shaders and document any necessary integration changes.
Consume output buffers without recomputing the same CPU work in JS; include all upload preparation and copies in timing.
Test callbacks, multiple renders, reads between updates and fallback paths.
Pass numerical and image checks on actual browser rendering.
tasks.verification: End-to-end tests, measured copy/read costs, matched draw work, bypass proof and screenshots.
tasks.excluded: Inferring GPU shader savings from CPU language changes.

tasks.title: Evaluate full-path performance across hardware and browsers
criteria: Use fixed benchmark versions and at least a second distinct hardware class for generalization.
Repeat paired full-path measurements, report uncertainty and retain unfavorable workloads.
Measure CPU, frame intervals, GPU diagnostics, startup, memory/GC and sustained behavior separately.
Run correctness before performance on every supported environment and report missing browser/device coverage.
tasks.verification: Raw reproducible datasets and per-environment verdicts; no pooled unrelated machines.
tasks.excluded: One universal speedup number inferred from a kernel or a single cloud GPU.

tasks.title: Audit compatibility, addon identity and long-running lifecycle behavior
criteria: Expand the pinned API inventory and upstream differential suite for implemented behavior.
Exercise supported addons, package consumers, hosting/Wasm initialization and TypeScript resolution.
Stress create/remove/reparent/release cycles, memory growth, callbacks and relevant context-loss behavior.
Document failures and fallback cost; keep unsupported ecosystem combinations explicit.
tasks.verification: Published compatibility matrix and long-run results with exact versions.
tasks.excluded: Marking untouched APIs as ported merely because JS forwarding works.

tasks.title: Publish the product verdict and bounded release-readiness decision
criteria: Evaluate the predeclared improvement and regression budgets against complete-path results.
Separate compatibility-facade and explicit ownership API outcomes, and JS structure gains from Rust gains.
Choose continue, narrow scope, pivot or stop with evidence; negative findings are valid completion.
Prepare versioned local artifacts and release notes only for verified scope; npm publication requires a separate decision.
tasks.verification: Reproducible report, source/data links, open limitations and explicit release/no-release rationale.
tasks.excluded: Automatic npm publication or full Three.js compatibility claims.

tasks.title: Validate reusable Rust engines, compatibility layers and renderer strategies
criteria: Pin fresh revisions and inspect WAMR3D, oneilltomhq/three-rs and eugenehp/threers; review three-rs/three and issue 19339 as design history.
Verify licenses and actual build/browser paths before considering code reuse; reproduce any performance claim used in a decision.
Compare state ownership, arbitrary JS property animation, numerical precision, callbacks, duplicate JS/Rust work and image/test infrastructure.
Compare a modified Three.js renderer adapter, an existing Rust scene/renderer core and a fresh bounded core; record integration/maintenance/compatibility costs.
tasks.verification: Source/license matrix, attempted builds/tests with blockers, representative measurements and reuse-versus-build decision before target architecture.
tasks.excluded: Importing old session implementations or treating pasted conversation performance numbers as reproduced evidence.

tasks.title: Extend Rust ownership through visibility, LOD and per-pass render lists
criteria: Proceed only if the M6 verdict supports expansion and fresh profiles justify this slice.
Keep camera, bounds, visibility and hierarchy in persistent state; produce opaque/transmissive/transparent lists with correct ordering.
Cover shadow passes, multiple cameras, LOD, layer masks and custom sorting/fallback contracts.
Retain optimized JS and upstream controls with matched visual quality.
tasks.verification: Numerical visibility/list oracle, multi-pass images, callbacks and repeated full-path hardware performance.
tasks.excluded: Claiming one main-camera visible list is a complete scene evaluator.

tasks.title: Consume prepared render plans and dirty buffers without scene recomputation
criteria: Define versioned handles/buffers for geometry, material, texture, draw/instance ranges and dirty uploads; avoid per-frame scene JSON.
Integrate a reviewed renderer input boundary that bypasses replaced traversal/culling/sorting/transform work.
Maintain material/shader behavior and public read/callback semantics or explicitly bounded fallbacks.
Prove replaced JS work is absent and include final upload/materialization costs in product timing.
tasks.verification: Bypass instrumentation, semantic and image differential tests, resource lifetime checks and whole-frame hardware comparison.
tasks.excluded: Assuming unmodified renderer.render(scene,camera) accepts an external prepared list.

tasks.title: Decide backend expansion and sustainable release scope from residual costs
criteria: Profile residual resource management, bindings, shader/TSL generation and command submission separately from GPU shader work.
Revisit adapter versus reusable Rust renderer strategy with licenses, supported ecosystem and upstream maintenance costs.
Move backend work only if useful costs justify the compatibility burden; preserve a documented stop option.
Publish release/support boundaries, upstream update strategy and reproducibility; keep npm publication a separate explicit decision.
tasks.verification: Cost-based ADR, compatibility matrix, cross-hardware evidence and maintainability/release checklist.
tasks.excluded: Automatic full renderer rewrite, unsupported ecosystem promises or npm publication.

tasks.title: Generate a standalone progress page and subsystem tile image from a bounded inventory
criteria: Deterministic HTML, JSON and SVG from one explicit inventory
Simple table, dark grouped tiles, evidence links and precise counting rules
Desktop/mobile inspection and CI freshness check
tasks.verification: Generator unit/freshness tests and browser inspection
tasks.excluded: Full Three.js percentage, copied GPL code, public deployment

tasks.title: Make ownership progress source-derived, simplify the README and prepare the animation pipeline
criteria: Extract actual pinned callable and field definitions with separate computation/authority status.
Publish a concise README and genuine progress history without incompatible trend claims.
Prepare repeatable animation/transform/palette workload, semantic oracle, cost diagnostics and a provisional boundary contract.
Verify and integrate the authorized dependency and current PRs into main; preserve open hardware/reuse/port gates.
tasks.verification: Source inventory/history tests, browser visuals, upstream oracle, raw diagnostics and exact-head main CI.
tasks.excluded: New Rust animation implementation, physical-GPU claims or paid runner provisioning.
